0.long_answer: Genomic studies of non-NF2 meningiomas have revealed that TRAF7, which stands for tumor necrosis factor receptor–associated factor 7, is mutated in nearly one-quarter of these tumors. The discovery of TRAF7 mutations has provided significant insights into the pathogenesis of meningiomas, particularly those that do not harbor NF2 mutations. These findings have helped classify meningiomas into molecular subgroups, with TRAF7 mutations being one of the key genetic alterations contributing to the development and progression of the tumor.
